verdict: Homebase: Choose Homebase when SMB hourly scheduling and time clocks priced per location is the job — not when you need restaurant-only WFM, multi-entity Deputy, or a core HRIS. Scores use the HR editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Free Basic for tiny hourly teams
Scheduling + time + light hiring in one SMB app
Published AI assistants on higher tiers
weaknesses: Payroll and hiring boosts are add-ons
bestFor: Small hourly businesses (retail, cafes, local services) that need scheduling + time in one app
Teams that want a free ≤10-employee starter before paying per location
Operators who may add payroll later rather than buying Gusto first
notIdealFor: Multi-entity mid-market WFM (Deputy) or deskless comms hubs (Connecteam)
Buyers whose primary job is core HRIS or structured ATS
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs
Hub / multi-module pricing complexity vs single-product floors
Mobile/frontline readiness vs desk-bound admin depth
Opaque contact-sales pricing vs transparent published seats
recommendation: Choose Homebase when SMB hourly scheduling and time clocks priced per location is the job — not when you need restaurant-only WFM, multi-entity Deputy, or a core HRIS. Compare Connecteam for deskless hubs, When I Work for cheap per-user scheduling, Deputy for mid-market compliance, and 7shifts for restaurants.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Homebase is the SMB hourly default for replacing paper schedules. Score reflects first-party packaging, not hands-on lab testing.
Primary job is frontline WFM (scheduling + time + light hiring). Scored inside WFM, not against ATS or core HRIS.
Scheduling, clocks, comms, and optional payroll/hiring are solid for SMB. Held at 8 vs Deputy’s deeper multi-location compliance.
POS/payroll connectors are marketed for hourly ops; adequate SMB depth, not an enterprise HCM graph.
Hourly mobile scheduling and clock-in are the product thesis — scored as WFM mobility.
Labor reporting on paid tiers is adequate for SMB; not enterprise WFM BI.
Per-location paid unlimited employees helps a growing shop; multi-brand/mid-market is a different shortlist.
Meaningful free Basic plus $24 annual location floor is strong; add-ons and extra locations raise TCO. Affiliate economics excluded.
Scheduling Assistant (Plus+) and Hiring/Payroll assistants are published — useful, plan-gated AI.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine HR editorial criteria using the category weights (hiring/workforce fit 15, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, value 12, mobile/frontline 10, scalability 9, analytics 8, AI 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ATS, core HRIS, payroll/benefits, people-platform, frontline WFM, time & attendance, SOP training, and LMS peers are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
